draft.title: Best power station for a refrigerator through a 24-hour outage
draft.subtitle: Which stations carry a full-size refrigerator for a day, from our runtime estimates
draft.excerpt: A full-size refrigerator uses 1,488 Wh a day. Of the stations in our data, the Elite 400 runs one for 52.15 hours (46.45 to 57.29 hours).
draft.body_md:
A full-size refrigerator uses 1,488 Wh a day in our data, about 62 W on average, and needs 2,600 W for a moment to start its compressor. Through a 24-hour outage that rules out the small stations: the [Yeti 500](/product/B0RPFX0002) runs one for 6.78 hours (6.04 to 7.45 hours) and cannot start it.

## How the refrigerator type changes the answer

The same station gives different hours to different refrigerators. On the [Explorer 1500 Ultra](/product/B0RPFX0007), a top-freezer model runs for 28.04 hours, a full-size model for 20.86 hours and a side-by-side model for 16.29 hours. Each is an estimate from rated capacity times 0.842 usable; [how we calculate](/how-we-calculate) shows where the range comes from.

The [Elite 400](/product/B0RPFX0010) is the station here that covers a French-door refrigerator for a full day on its estimate: 45.46 hours (40.49 to 49.94 hours). The [AC180P](/product/B0RPFX0006) gives a full-size refrigerator 19.56 hours, and the [DELTA 3 Max Plus](/product/B0RPFX0015) gives it 27.81 hours.

{{picks:power-station-for-refrigerator}}

## Recharging between outages

Solar shortens the wait for the next outage. See [what charges the Elite 400](/compat/bluetti-elite-400) and [what charges the DELTA 3 Max Plus](/compat/ecoflow-delta-3-max-plus) for the panels that fit each, with the cold-weather assumptions beside every verdict. The [refrigerator runtime page](/runtime/refrigerator) lists every station we estimate.

faqs.question: Where do the hours come from?
faqs.answer: From each maker's published capacity and our usable-capacity rule (rated capacity times 0.842 unless a measured figure exists), divided by the refrigerator's average draw.

draft.title: Best power station for Starlink and home Wi-Fi in an outage
draft.subtitle: Router and modem, Starlink Mini and Starlink Standard are three different loads
draft.excerpt: A router and modem draw about 16 W, Starlink Mini about 40 W and Starlink Standard about 100 W in our data, so the same station gives each a very different number of hours.
draft.body_md:
A Wi-Fi router and cable modem draw about 16 W together in our data, Starlink Mini about 40 W and Starlink Standard about 100 W. That spread decides the station size more than anything else.

## One station, three loads

On the [Explorer 1500 Ultra](/product/B0RPFX0007), the router and modem run for 80.83 hours, Starlink Mini for 32.33 hours and Starlink Standard for 12.93 hours (11.52 to 14.21 hours). Each load is counted on its own; running two at once shortens both.

Through a 12-hour night, Starlink Standard needs a station like the [AC180P](/product/B0RPFX0006), which gives it 12.12 hours (10.8 to 13.32 hours), or the [DELTA 3 Max Plus](/product/B0RPFX0015) at 17.24 hours. The [Power 1000 Mini](/product/B0RPFX0004) gives it 8.49 hours, so it suits Starlink Mini better: 21.22 hours.

The [Elite 400](/product/B0RPFX0010) runs the router and modem for 202.08 hours on its estimate.

If someone in the house sleeps with a small bedside therapy machine, the kind many people with apnea use every night, it draws about as much as Starlink Mini, so the [Explorer 1500 Ultra](/product/B0RPFX0007) covers it for 32.33 hours.

{{picks:power-station-for-starlink}}

## Charging and the math

Panels that fit each station are on its compatibility page: [the AC180P](/compat/bluetti-ac180p) and [the Elite 400](/compat/bluetti-elite-400). Every estimate uses rated capacity times 0.842 unless a measured figure exists; see [how we calculate](/how-we-calculate). The full tables are on [the Starlink Standard page](/runtime/starlink-standard) and [the router page](/runtime/wifi-router-modem).

faqs.question: Can I run Starlink and the router together?
faqs.answer: Yes, but the hours shrink: our estimates give each load on its own, so add the draws before you compare stations.

faqs.question: Why does Starlink Mini change the station size?
faqs.answer: It draws about 40 W against about 100 W for the Standard kit, so the same station lasts more than twice as long.

draft.title: Best power station for a sump pump: which models start a 1/2 HP pump, and for how long
draft.subtitle: Starting the pump comes first; hours come second
draft.excerpt: A 1/2 HP sump pump needs 3,200 W to start and draws about 1,050 W running in our data. Only some stations start it.
draft.body_md:
A 1/2 HP sump pump needs 3,200 W for a moment to start and draws about 1,050 W while it runs, in our data. A station that cannot start it is no help, however large its battery.

## Which stations start it

The [Elite 400](/product/B0RPFX0010) starts it and carries it for 3.08 hours of continuous pumping (2.74 to 3.38 hours). The [Explorer 1500 Ultra](/product/B0RPFX0007) starts it and gives 1.23 hours, and the [DELTA 3 Max Plus](/product/B0RPFX0015) gives 1.64 hours. The [AC180P](/product/B0RPFX0006) carries the running draw but does not start it in our data, and neither does the [C1000 Gen 2](/product/B0RPFX0017).

These hours treat the pump as running the whole time, the worst case, because no duty cycle is published. A pump that cycles runs longer; [how we calculate](/how-we-calculate) explains the range.

The same station keeps the circulator pump on a hot-water baseboard heating loop turning, so the house stays warm; the [Elite 400](/product/B0RPFX0010) is the one to pick for that.

{{picks:power-station-for-sump-pump}}

Plug the pump straight into the station's AC outlet; connecting a power station to your home's wiring is a job for a licensed electrician.

## Recharging

See [what charges the Elite 400](/compat/bluetti-elite-400) and [what charges the DELTA 3 Max Plus](/compat/ecoflow-delta-3-max-plus).

faqs.question: What matters more, capacity or surge?
faqs.answer: Surge: a station must cover the 3,200 W start before its capacity matters.

draft.title: Will this solar panel work with my power station? The cold-voltage check
draft.subtitle: A panel's voltage rises in the cold; a fit needs headroom on the coldest morning
draft.excerpt: We check every panel and station pair at -40 C with at least 5% headroom under the station's maximum PV input. Some popular pairs fail.
draft.body_md:
A solar panel's open-circuit voltage rises as it gets colder, so a pair that works in July can exceed the station's limit on a January morning. We design for -40 C, apply the code factor when a panel's temperature coefficient is unknown, and call a pair a fit only with at least 5% headroom under the station's maximum PV voltage.

## Pairs that fit

The [400W Lightweight Portable Solar Panel](/product/B0RPFX0047) reaches 45.686 V cold against the 60 V input of the [C2000 Gen 2](/product/B0RPFX0018) and the [Elite 300](/product/B0RPFX0009), so it fits both. Its compatibility is listed on [the C2000 Gen 2 page](/compat/anker-solix-c2000-gen-2) and [the Elite 300 page](/compat/bluetti-elite-300).

The smaller Flash300 takes 45 V at most, and the [175W Rigid Solar Panel](/product/B0RPFX0049) fits it two in parallel at 29.644 V cold.

{{compat:zendure-superbase-v4600}}

## Pairs that do not

The [SORA 500 (500W Solar Panel)](/product/B0RPFX0055) reaches 61.375 V cold, above the 60 V input of the [AC180P](/product/B0RPFX0006), so we do not call it a fit. See [what charges the AC180P](/compat/bluetti-ac180p) for the panels that do, and [how we calculate](/how-we-calculate) for the cold-voltage method.

faqs.answer: It is the conservative design temperature we use for every verdict, so a fit holds on the coldest morning most readers will see.
